ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: (2018 Central and Southern Jiangxi Five-School Joint Examination) As shown in the figure, this is an electric field line in the electric field produced by a certain point charge Q. A and B are two points on the electric field line. When an electron moves from A to B along the electric field line with a certain velocity, its kinetic energy increases, so it can be judged that ()
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The direction of the electric field line is from B pointing to A

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, there is an electric field line in the electric field produced by a certain point charge Q, and A and B are two points on the electric field line. During the process in which an electron moves from A to B along the electric field line with a certain velocity, its kinetic energy increases. Based on this process, what can be judged about the direction of this electric field line?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The direction of the electric field line is from B pointing to A
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an electric field line in the electric field produced by a certain point charge Q, with points A and B marked on this electric field line; the problem statement says that the electron moves from A to B along this electric field line. Reasoning: During the process in which the electron moves from A to B, its kinetic energy increases, indicating that the electric field force does positive work on the electron, so the direction of the electric field force on the electron is in the same direction as the displacement A→B. The electron carries negative charge, and the force direction on a negative charge is opposite to the electric field direction, so the electric field direction should be opposite to A→B. Therefore, the direction of this electric field line is from B pointing to A.
